svg.title: Gaussian data make spacetime a hyperbolic strip
svg.desc: Left: the (m, s) half-plane for q = N(0,1). Geodesics between pairs of points anchored at s = 0.08 are semi-ellipses whose apex grows with the separation d; for d = 3.6 the apex passes s = 1, above which no posterior exists. Two PF-ODE paths are drawn as dashed quarter ellipses; only the one with x = sqrt 2 has the geodesic shape. Right: DiffED against Euclidean distance on a log axis. It follows the logarithmic law 2 sqrt2 log(d / sqrt2 s) once d exceeds the anchor noise, and is capped by the length of the path through q itself.
svg.text: q = N(0, 1): spacetime is a hyperbolic strip
s > 1: not a posterior of any x_t
Grey, d = 3.6: the semi-ellipse passes s = 1, so the true geodesic must run along the top edge.
Euclidean distance d between the two points
DiffED(d), both endpoints at noise s = 0.08
via q itself: bound on the true DiffED
